title: Failed to remove PowerToys folder when updating from stable to Preview
author: maisondasilva

linked_work.relevance: Related per-user installer regression from the same stable-to-preview upgrade area, but focused on duplicate Burn bundle planning rather than scheduled-task cleanup.

judgment.rationale: The report gives a stable-to-Preview per-user upgrade path, the exact warning text, and a maintainer confirmation that the warning is reproducible across multiple versions. Repository inspection finds the matching custom action and a deletion loop that can skip remaining tasks while mutating the live Task Scheduler collection.
evidence: The issue reproduces on a per-user stable-to-Preview upgrade and shows the exact scheduled-task folder warning in an attached screenshot.
Maintainer niels9001 commented that the same warning has appeared for multiple versions and offered a reproduction machine.
installer/PowerToysSetupCustomActionsVNext/CustomAction.cpp::RemoveScheduledTasksCA logs the exact warning after deleting tasks and then failing to delete the PowerToys task folder.
RemoveScheduledTasksCA captures task count once and deletes tasks while iterating get_Item(i + 1), which can skip or fail later items if the underlying collection shrinks during deletion.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve a focused scheduled-task cleanup design and verify the collection-mutation hypothesis with a maintainer-side reproduction trace.

fix_assessment.rationale: A product-side code fix is applicable in RemoveScheduledTasksCA, but one reproduction with the remaining task names and HRESULT would confirm whether collection mutation is the only failing path.

proposed_fixes.title: Snapshot scheduled-task names before deletion and only remove the folder after the snapshot is drained
proposed_fixes.root_cause: RemoveScheduledTasksCA deletes tasks from the same IRegisteredTaskCollection that it is still indexing, so a later task can survive the loop and block DeleteFolder even though the code thinks it processed every entry.
plan: Read the PowerToys task names into a stable local list before issuing any DeleteTask calls.
Delete each named task from that snapshot, logging missing-task and HRESULT cases explicitly instead of depending on the live collection index after mutation.
Attempt folder deletion only after the snapshot is exhausted, and keep the warning path specific to the remaining failing task or permission error.
verification: Create an upgrade scenario with more than one PowerToys scheduled task and confirm every task is deleted before DeleteFolder runs.
Verify the warning no longer appears for the stable-to-Preview per-user upgrade path while genuinely undeletable tasks still surface a precise warning.
Confirm the fix does not change successful cleanup for installs that already have zero or one scheduled task.

confidence.rationale: The custom-action control flow matches the symptom closely, but a single maintainer repro should confirm whether a surviving task, access denial, or cross-channel coexistence is the live failing branch.

issue_context.summary: A per-user upgrade from stable PowerToys to Preview can stop with a warning that the PowerToys scheduled-task folder could not be removed.
known_information: The reporter supplied a stable-to-Preview per-user upgrade path and a screenshot of the exact warning.
A maintainer reported the same warning across multiple install and uninstall attempts on other versions.
The warning text maps directly to RemoveScheduledTasksCA in the installer custom actions.
inferences: A leftover scheduled task is more likely than a missing folder because the custom action warns only after attempting folder deletion.
The live collection iteration is a plausible reason a remaining task survives even when the loop starts with the correct count.
issue_context.analysis: This is already reproducible enough for a maintainer-side cleanup investigation, so the next uncertainty-reducing action is local reproduction rather than asking the reporter for a generic log bundle.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the complete issue body, both comments, labels, screenshot attachment, and timeline activity.
Inspected installer/PowerToysSetupCustomActionsVNext/CustomAction.cpp::RemoveScheduledTasksCA and confirmed it emits the issue's exact warning text.
Compared the symptom to related installer issue #50087 and kept them separate because #50111 is in the scheduled-task custom action path rather than the duplicate Burn related-bundle plan path.

reproduce.title: Capture which PowerToys scheduled task survives stable-to-Preview cleanup
reproduce.version_requirement: PowerToys stable installed per-user, then upgrade with a current Preview x64 installer
prerequisites: A per-user stable installation created with WinGet or another user-scope bundle path
Task Scheduler access to inspect the \PowerToys folder before and after upgrade
setup: Confirm whether the \PowerToys Task Scheduler folder contains more than one task before starting the upgrade.
Prepare installer logging so the warning timestamp and any custom-action HRESULT can be correlated.
steps: Run the Preview installer over the stable per-user installation.
When the warning appears, inspect the \PowerToys Task Scheduler folder and note any remaining task names.
Correlate the remaining tasks with RemoveScheduledTasksCA logging to see whether get_Item/DeleteTask stopped early or a specific DeleteTask/DeleteFolder call failed.
Repeat once with only a single scheduled task present, if possible, to distinguish collection mutation from a generic permission failure.
reproduce.expected_result: All PowerToys scheduled tasks should be deleted before the folder delete runs; if one remains, the trace should identify the surviving task and failing call so the cleanup fix can stay bounded.

actions.label: Approve scheduled-task cleanup fix design
actions.note: Keeps the work bounded to the installer custom action that deletes PowerToys scheduled tasks during upgrade cleanup.
